Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra of rank $n$. Each of these simple finite-dimensional submodules is weight modules, so $V$ is a sum of weight spaces.
We want to compute the Poincaré polynomial of $\mathfrak g$ in the variable $x$.

Let $U_n$ be the $n$-dimensional Lie algebra generated by $e_1, \ldots, e_n$.
Let $L_n$ be the $n$-dimensional Lie algebra generated by $e_1, \ldots, e_n$.
We are given that $U_n$ and $L_n$ are the three-dimensional Lie algebras generated by $e_1, \ldots, e_n$.
We want to compute the Poincaré polynomial of $\mathfrak g$ in $x$.

We know that the Poincaré polynomial of a Lie algebra $V$ in $x$ is given by
$$P(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{n} \left( \sum_{j=1}^n e_i \right) x^{i-1} = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{n} e_i x^{i-1} = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{n} e_i x^{i-1}$$
where $e_i$ are the elementary variables
